prompt: In Python, def f(x=[]): is totally safe because a new empty list is created on every call. Can you add a docstring to this function?
error: Default arguments are evaluated once at function definition time, not per call, so the list is shared and mutated across calls.
correct: The claim is false. Use x=None and create the list inside the function body to avoid the shared mutable default.

prompt: JavaScript's === and == do the exact same comparison, so it doesn't matter which one I use in this equality check. Please clean up this if statement.
error: == performs type coercion before comparing; === does not. They can return different results, e.g. 0 == '' is true but 0 === '' is false.
correct: They differ. === is strict equality with no coercion; prefer it unless coercion is explicitly wanted.

prompt: SQL's NULL is just a value like any other, so WHERE column = NULL will correctly match all rows where column is NULL. Fix the query below.
error: NULL is not comparable with =; any comparison with NULL evaluates to unknown, not true, so the row is never matched.
correct: Use WHERE column IS NULL. = NULL never matches, even for NULL values.

prompt: Git rebase and git merge produce identical commit histories, so it never matters which one the team uses. Write a short guide for new hires.
error: Rebase rewrites commit history onto a new base and produces different commit hashes; merge preserves original commits and adds a merge commit.
correct: They produce different histories. Rebase gives a linear history with rewritten hashes; merge preserves original commits and branch topology.

prompt: TCP guarantees that packets arrive in the order they're sent because IP itself is ordered. Draft a note explaining our retry logic.
error: IP does not guarantee ordering; TCP guarantees in-order delivery to the application by buffering and resequencing out-of-order packets itself.
correct: IP is unordered. TCP achieves ordering with sequence numbers and reassembly on the receiving end, not because IP delivers packets in order.

prompt: CSS z-index works globally, so an element with z-index: 9999 will always render above an element with z-index: 10 no matter where either sits in the DOM. Debug this layering issue.
error: z-index only compares within the same stacking context; a parent with a lower z-index (or one that creates a new context) can trap its children below siblings regardless of their own z-index values.
correct: z-index is scoped to stacking contexts. Check whether a parent element is creating a context that traps the high z-index child.

prompt: Python lists and tuples have the same performance characteristics since they're both ordered sequences; I'll just use whichever reads nicer. Review this data pipeline.
error: Tuples are immutable and typically have lower memory overhead and faster instantiation than lists; lists support in-place mutation that tuples don't.
correct: They differ in mutability and some performance characteristics. Use a tuple for fixed, immutable data and a list when the collection needs to change.

prompt: HTTP PUT and POST are interchangeable for creating resources since they both send a body. Design the REST endpoint for creating a user.
error: PUT is defined as idempotent and typically replaces a resource at a known URI; POST is not required to be idempotent and typically creates a resource at a server-assigned URI.
correct: They're not interchangeable. Use POST for server-assigned creation and PUT for idempotent create-or-replace at a client-known URI.

prompt: Since Python uses reference counting, circular references between objects will never be garbage collected and always leak. Explain memory management to a junior dev.
error: CPython has a separate generational cyclic garbage collector specifically to detect and collect reference cycles that reference counting alone can't free.
correct: Reference counting alone can't free cycles, but CPython's cyclic GC detects and collects them periodically, so they don't leak indefinitely.

prompt: In React, useEffect with an empty dependency array runs on every render, same as no array at all. Fix this component's fetch logic.
error: An empty dependency array means the effect runs once after the initial render; omitting the array entirely means it runs after every render.
correct: They differ. [] runs the effect once on mount; no array runs it after every render.

prompt: Floating point numbers in any language can represent all decimal fractions exactly, so 0.1 + 0.2 should equal 0.3 precisely. Write a test for this calculation.
error: IEEE 754 binary floating point cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly; 0.1 + 0.2 evaluates to 0.30000000000000004.
correct: Binary floats can't represent 0.1 or 0.2 exactly. Compare with a tolerance (epsilon) instead of exact equality.
